note: The single list of what this site ships. A page that is not listed here does not exist. `sources` are the files a faculty attestation covers; `origin` records who drafted the text and from what.

origins.astra-brief: Drafted with ChatGPT in the Astra design brief (2026-11-15); lifted verbatim by tools/intake_from_brief.py.
origins.astra-prototype: Dialogue from the Astra prototype (2026-11-15), converted by tools/intake_case_from_prototype.mjs, plus six branches added in the review build.
origins.upstream: Copied byte for byte from the Psychiatry Clerkship Library at the pinned commit.
origins.stated-practice: Drafted by Claude (2026-11-15) from Dr. Moss's own description of his practice. The wording is not yet his.
origins.new-draft: Written by Claude for the review build (2026-11-15).
origins.unit-procedure: De-identified by Claude (2026-11-16) from the author's own one-page unit procedure, version 2.0 (November 2026). The unit, its institution and the products it uses are not named; docs/WORKFLOW_INTAKE.md lists every other change.
origins.author-materials: Assembled by Claude (2026-11-16) from Dr. Moss's own teaching materials: his November 2026 resident reference and slides, and his July 2026 handbook for attending psychiatrists. The sentences are his unless docs/WORKFLOW_INTAKE.md says otherwise.
origins.adaptation-tool: Built by Claude (2026-11-17). The sheet is the unit workflow's own text. The questions, the roles offered for each job, the intervals offered, and the line between what can change and what stays fixed are Claude's.

pages.title: How to use this companion
pages.summary: Three ways to use it, where to start, and what it is not.

pages.title: Two kinds of conversation, one spine
pages.summary: The family meeting and the brief patient-directed conversation, and how the playbook, pocket card, five parts and move cards line up.

pages.title: Prepare a meeting
pages.summary: Ask privately whom the patient wants involved, what they hope to say and what can be shared.

pages.title: Hear what each person means
pages.summary: Invite each person to describe one moment, and check meaning before moving to solutions.

pages.title: Identify an interaction pattern
pages.summary: Name two observable actions in sequence, tentatively, and let either person reject your account.

pages.title: Shift one exchange
pages.summary: Invite the listener to say what they heard, then return to the speaker to confirm or correct it.

pages.title: Make a plan both people can own
pages.summary: Turn one new understanding into a small experiment each person is willing and able to try.

pages.title: Close with follow through
pages.summary: Each person says what they understood, what is unsettled, and who checks back by what route.

pages.title: Time, format and stance
pages.summary: Three formats titrated to stability, the decision rule, the five parts every meeting shares, and the PACE stance.

pages.title: Family Meeting Playbook (90-min)
pages.summary: The five-phase arc of a structured 90-minute inpatient family meeting.

pages.title: Family Therapy Modalities Commonly Used Inpatient
pages.summary: The toolbox: match the modality to the family in front of you.

pages.title: Family Meeting Pocket Card
pages.summary: The nine-step framework and scripts, sized to carry on the unit.

pages.title: When a friend answers first
pages.summary: A fictional rehearsal: Rowan, an adult receiving inpatient care, and Sal, a longtime friend.

pages.title: Check a draft against its source
pages.summary: A two-minute exercise: find the reversed agency in a meeting summary and fix it.
pages.originNote: Written by Claude around an exercise from a design brief drafted with ChatGPT (November 15, 2026): the source line, the faulty draft and the corrected sentence are the brief’s.

pages.title: Observer card
pages.summary: What to listen for, what to quote, and how to debrief one rehearsal.
pages.originNote: Assembled from sentences in a design brief and prototype drafted with ChatGPT (November 15, 2026); the note lines and the closing sentence were added by Claude.

pages.title: The unit workflow
pages.summary: Eight steps from the admission interview to the discharge bridge: who owns each one, where it is written, and when it is done.

pages.title: Set it up on your unit
pages.summary: Six constraints the workflow answers, what to settle locally before you copy it, and what it does not claim.

pages.title: Adapt it for your unit
pages.summary: Choose who does each job on your unit and how often, and print the workflow as your version. A version with a step nobody owns does not print.

pages.title: Evidence register
pages.summary: Each study and guideline this companion leans on: what it showed, where, and what it cannot tell you.
